changes.reason: The current 1–4 cut lies inside the entangled Sr 4p / O 2s block, so the gate does not honour it. Excluding all 5 semicore bands cuts across a 10.76 eV gap, which the gate honours. num_wann goes to 12 and num_bands to 47, per validate_deck.

diagnosis:
The construction fails because of where the bottom of the spectrum is cut, not because of the gauge or the windows. The deck excludes bands 1–4 (Sr 4s and Sr 4p). But Sr 4p (bands 2–5, from −19.3 to −15.65 eV) is entangled with the O 2s band: band 4 reaches 0.35 eV into band 5. The gate therefore does not honour the cut and counts every excluded occupied state as missing. That alone sets occupied_manifold_is_represented to 0.499 and band_distance_from_parent to 6.4 eV. The same goes for every frontier run: all ten changed only the projectability thresholds, and all landed on exactly 0.4992 / 6.413. Those knobs cannot reach the bottom-exclusion problem.

The eta_2 failure has the same source. In band_error_by_energy, nearly all of the 119 meV comes from DFT band 5, matched to Wannier band 1 (the O 2s / Sr 4p mixture near −15 eV, up to 1.07 eV off). The model has a single O 2s function to stand in for a block in which it is entangled with the excluded Sr 4p. The O 2p valence bands (eta 9 meV and 3 meV) and the frozen conduction bands are already reproduced well.

validate_deck lists the possible cuts. Excluding 1 band (gap 15.66 eV) and excluding 5 bands (gap 10.76 eV) are both honoured. Excluding 5 removes the whole isolated semicore block (Sr 4s, Sr 4p, O 2s) at once. That leaves the target as the O 2p valence plus the Sr 4d/5s conduction: 12 functions in 47 bands. Every kept band then lies above a clean gap.
